description.narrative: (1) The Social Protection Floor (SPF) for the Philippines was adopted on 20 April 2023 by the National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) Board chaired by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The SPF recommendations were drafted in consultation with the Tripartite Executive Committee (TEC) of the National Tripartite Industrial Peace Council (NTIPC). Key SPF recommendations include ensuring the full implementation of Universal Health Care act, enhancing benefits of existing programmes (i.e. unemployment insurance, livelihood programmes, reintegration programmes and portability of benefits for Filipino migrant workers, insurance subsidy for workers in the informal sector), extending coverage of social pension and conditional cash transfer children beneficiaries under Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps); addressing administrative issues in benefit payments; and including special programmes in times of emergencies. Moreover, the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-28 includes as one of its key strategies to strengthen social protection the establishment of a standard menu of rationalized programs for the social protection floor guarantees. (2) The Social Protection Plan 2023-28 for the Philippines was adopted on 27 July 2023, by the Social Development Committee at Cabinet level which is chaired by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The Plan includes as its first strategic focus "Implementing the Social Protection Floor". This will include the implementation of strategic initiatives to ensure comprehensive income security and universal health care for all children, active age and elderly, providing everyone guaranteed access to a menu of SP programs during various life-cycle shocks and risks. For Results 1 and 2: The ILO provided technical advisory services in the updating of the Social Protection Floor assessment matrices as well as the conduct of sectoral and multi-stakeholder consultations from 2018 to 2022. Consultations included workers’ and employers’ organizations as well as six (6) Basic Sectoral Councils of the National Anti-Poverty Commission (NAPC). The results of the Assessment Based National Dialogue exercise, facilitated by the ILO, from 2014 to 2016 also served as a major input in the updating exercise towards the finalization of the elements of the proposed social protection floor in the Philippines.

description.narrative: 1. To support and progress on the ratification process, in Aug 2023, the new Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) (created in 2021) formally communicated to DFA its support for ratification of C190. DMW was not part of the 2019-21 process of getting endorsement from the executive agencies for ratification of C190. Recognizing that C190 is relevant and important for migrant workers, endorsement from DMW was sought by DFA and DOLE Technical Working Committee and social partners on C190 Ratification, which will allow the process to proceed with DFA endorsing the ratification to the President so that this can be transmitted to the Senate for concurrence. In Jan 2023, the consolidated House Resolution 650 was also approved, calling for the immediate ratification of C190 by the President and concurrence by the Senate. In Nov 2022, a "Parliamentarians and Advocates' Campaign to Ratify C190" was launched by legislators from the Lower House. In 2023, two Senate resolutions (SR) have been filed: SR 726 by the Women, Children and Gender Equality Committee; and SR 456 by the Labor Committee, urging the President to ratify C190. The Women and Gender Equality Committee has also formally requested the Senate Foreign Affairs Committee (in charge of ratification matters) to support the ratification. 2. Following the HLTM, women labour leaders and trade union organizers launched in 2023 a new alliance of women workers and submitted a collective women workers' HLTM sub-report on FOA issues in the Philippines and called for the engendering of the 15-Point Labour Agenda, including a more expanded discussion on the gender impacts of free trade and how rights-based trade mechanisms can be leveraged to improve FOA in the Philippines. Women workers also issued a concerted campaign call to not only ensure ratification of C190 but also to come up with post-C190 ratification action plans and strategies for implementation. 1. ILO spearheaded a series of five stakeholders’ consultations in March 2022 which made recommendations on the IRR of the DMW Law (R.A. 11641), and on institutional programmes and operations of DMW, including the importance of ratifying C190 to strengthen protection of OFWS against violence and harassment. From 2022 until 1st half of 2023, ILO held several meetings and joint activities with DMW, which included advocacy to strengthen gender and ending-VAW programmes and mechanisms of DMW, and the need to ratify and effectively implement C190, and conducting joint trainings for DMW and migration-related agencies on C190 and international labour, migration and recruitment standards. 2. ILO provided extensive technical support to the legislators to advance the formal process towards ratification, including in the development and submission of all relevant resolutions. 3. ILO supported the parliamentarians‘ campaign to ratify C190 launched by legislators in November 2022. 4. In 2022 until 1st half of 2023, ILO continued to collaborate with tripartite-plus partners in raising awareness and increasing understanding, providing C190 IECs (including translation into Filipino), and assisting in formulation of advocacy plans on C190 ratification e.g. 2020 16-day campaign on ending-VAW and International Migrants’ Day (Nov 25-Dec 18, 2022); launching of the Transnational Union of Filipino Domestic and Care Workers (Dec 2022); training of women workers on C190, gender-related standards, and ILO gender transformative agenda (March 2023; jointly with Commission on Human Rights and trade unions); training of trade unionists and strategic planning on C190 advocacy (April 2023, with TUCP).

description.narrative: Mechanism for gender, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) in TVET planning and delivery is adopted at TESDA as well as among government agencies and organizations involved in the implementation of lifelong learning mechanisms. The ILO supported a recognized national NGO expert on disability inclusion called the Project Inclusion Network (PIN) which is linked to ILO’s Global Business and Disability Network (GBDN), in pursuing a partnership arrangement with TESDA aimed at institutionalizing disability inclusion in TVET delivery. ILO also supported the "Review of Policies and Perceptions of Persons with Disabilities on Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) in the Philippines" as basis for arriving at recommendations to enhance access, engagement, and assistance for disabled individuals within the TVET framework. Based on this review, ILO developed a customized Toolkit for TVET Trainers, centered on facilitating effective disability inclusion. This Toolkit aims to equip TVET trainers with resources, strategies, and insights to foster a more supportive learning environment that accommodates individuals with disabilities. ILO support also includes a capacity-building program for TVET Trainers aimed at enhancing their proficiency in promoting accessible and comprehensive education for disabled learners. ILO's pilot implementation of inclusive, area-based lifelong learning approaches in the Visayas regions focused on learners or beneficiaries coming from indigenous peoples and their communities (Tubungan and Libacao, Region 6), women and youth (Basey, Region 8 and the cities of Cebu, Mandaue and Lapu-Lapu, Region 7).
